reasons: Deviation is correctly characterized: Section 9(b) as drafted warrants performance 'to industry standards' and freedom from utility-affecting errors but contains no professional/workmanlike services warranty, no conformance-to-documentation warranty with a stated duration, and no repair/replace/refund remedy; the rationale also correctly observes that the Section 13 disclaimer expressly carves out the Agreement's express warranties, so no edit to p0062 was needed.

Redline is a valid, minimal insertion: new clauses (xii)-(xiii) hang correctly off the p0032 lead-in ('Kubient represents, warrants and covenants that:'), leave existing text untouched, and reach the preferred position (professional and workmanlike performance; 12 months for software deliverables and 90 days for services; repair, replacement, re-performance or refund at Vendor's option).

Directionally pro-customer: the added warranty is additive and expressly non-exclusive ('in addition to, and does not limit, Customer's other rights and remedies'), so the new 90-day/12-month periods cannot be read to cut back the existing unlimited warranties in (ii) and (vi), and the remedy is not made an exclusive remedy.

Comment is accurate, concise, in the required voice, cites the playbook position and offers the 90-day software fallback; deterministic checks (operation applies; period ≥ 90 days) are consistent with the text.

Minor improvement (not disqualifying): the remedy sentence is drafted as covering breach of 'the warranties in this Section 9(b)' generally rather than only the new conformance warranty — narrowing it to clause (xiii) would remove any counterparty argument that it channels remedies for the IP, security and compliance warranties.
